environmentalPersistence: Low — tropospheric half-life ~22 days; highly reactive; formed continuously from NOₓ + VOC + sunlight

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate — chronic ozone reduces carbon assimilation and allocates resources to detox
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Strong — ozone-induced chloroplast damage; characteristic stippled or flecked chlorosis pattern
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Strong — surface necrosis with distinctive tan/bronze flecking pattern
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Moderate — ozone induces anthocyanin as part of oxidative stress response
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Moderately inhibited — carbon starvation from reduced photosynthesis
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Older mature leaves most affected — more open stomata and longer exposure history

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Strong — 40–65% at typical elevated ozone concentrations
physiologyEffects.photosyntheticRate: Significantly reduced — direct damage to photosynthetic apparatus
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Complex — ozone induces stomatal opening (allowing more ozone entry) then closure as damage accumulates
physiologyEffects.membranePermeability: Strongly increased — ozone is one of the most powerful oxidants to interact with plasma membrane

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Extremely strong — ozone itself is a reactive oxygen species; generates apoplastic ROS burst immediately upon stomatal entry
molecularEffects.lipidPeroxidation: Very strong — MDA accumulation is among the highest of all 40 chemicals
molecularEffects.anthocyaninInduction: Moderate — ozone stress anthocyanin well documented

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Moderate — ozone affects foliar microbiome significantly; rhizosphere less so
microbiomeEffects.fungalEffect: Foliar fungal pathogens may increase on ozone-weakened tissue
microbiomeEffects.rhizosphereStability: Mildly to moderately destabilized via altered root exudates

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: Poor — ozone damage is cumulative; necrotic stippling is permanent
temporalDynamics.acclimation: Partial — antioxidant enzyme upregulation provides partial adaptation
temporalDynamics.sensitization: Mild — prior ozone exposure primes antioxidant response

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → tan/bronze stippling (characteristic) → chlorosis → confluent necrosis
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Adaxial (upper) leaf surface of older leaves — most distinctive
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Upper surface stippling spreading to whole leaf
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Adaxial stippling/flecking — THE diagnostic visual signature of ozone damage in field conditions; unlike any other chemical in this simulator
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Very strong — among highest MDA signal in the simulator; SA peak secondary indicator
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Stippling is permanent; new leaves are healthy if source removed

synergies.synergyNote: O₃ + NO₂ creates photochemical smog cycle. O₃ + SO₂ creates the most damaging acid rain + oxidant combination. O₃ + ethylene accelerates senescence dramatically (senescent tissue more vulnerable to oxidative attack).
synergies.antagonismNote: Elevated CO₂ reduces stomatal aperture, reducing ozone uptake — partial protection. But ozone damage reduces CO₂ assimilation, partially canceling CO₂ benefit.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Tropospheric ozone formed from NOₓ + VOC + sunlight — summer smog days, downwind of cities. NOT the same as stratospheric ozone (ozone layer). One of the most important air pollutants for agriculture globally.
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Not applied intentionally — major agricultural pollutant; costs ~$11 billion/year in US crop losses alone
educationalContext.humanToxicity: High — lung irritant; triggers asthma; EPA standard: 70 ppb 8-hour average
educationalContext.climateLink: Climate change increases ozone formation — hotter temperatures and more sunlight accelerate photochemical reactions. Food security impact of rising ozone is projected to worsen with climate change.
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Primarily outdoor — formed in atmosphere; low indoor (reacts with surfaces quickly)
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Air quality alerts that say 'Sensitive groups should avoid outdoor activities' — that's ozone. The brown haze visible over cities in summer. Directly relevant to outdoor exercise and asthma.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Urban smog, crop yield losses, respiratory disease, climate-ozone feedback
